notes.claim: The 4 to 20 mA loop is a 0 to 100 percent scale, and its straight-line conversion is y = mx + b.
A 12 mA signal from a differential-pressure cell is 50% pressure difference but 71% flow rate.
A function is a rule that operates on an input and produces a single output from that input.
Instrument scaling uses a straight-line rule, y = mx + b, that turns each input value into one output value.
The input to a function is the independent variable and the output is the dependent variable.
A function gives a single output for any input, so on its graph each input meets the curve at one height.
A horizontal line that cuts the graph of y = x² more than once shows two different inputs giving the same output, so that function is many-to-one.
A straight-line rule y = mx + b is used to convert 4 to 20 mA instrument signals to real-world values.
Power depends upon the square of the current, which is why high-power applications are advised to minimise the current.
The generalised propeller law states that ship engine load is proportional to the cube of the propeller's rotational speed.
Current is cut in half if resistance doubles, which is the one-over shape; plotting pressure against volume for a gas (Boyle's law) gives a hyperbola.
For differential-pressure flow measurement the pressure difference is proportional to the square of the flow, so flow is found from the square root of the pressure difference.
Fan power goes with the cube of speed: slowing a fan to 50% speed reduces the power used to 12.5% (i3, the half-speed puzzle).
The propeller law works well in steady running at high speed and load but breaks down at partial loading, such as at a slower speed, so it is taught as a model (i3).
A function's domain is the set of values allowed for the input, and its range is the set of values the function takes as output.
The domain includes the real inputs that would not cause an undefined operation, such as dividing by zero or taking the square root of a negative number.
A 12 mA signal on a 4 to 20 mA loop from a differential-pressure cell is 50% pressure difference but 71% flow, because the square root of 0.5 is 0.707.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit expects learners to identify the domain, range and asymptotes of a given function.
i4: a vertical asymptote is a vertical line that a graph approaches but never crosses, as y = 1/x does with x = 0.
i4: a horizontal asymptote is a horizontal line that a graph approaches as the input increases or decreases without bound, as y = 1/x does with y = 0.
i4: the poles of a rational function are the inputs where its denominator is zero, the points where it is not defined, such as 0 for 1/x.
Adding or subtracting a constant k to a function shifts its graph up or down by k units.
Adding or subtracting a constant k to the x term shifts the graph left or right along the x-axis.
The horizontal shift direction is a common trap: the misconception is to shift right because the 3 in f(x + 3) is positive.
Multiplying a function by a positive constant stretches or compresses its graph vertically.
Multiplying all outputs by minus 1 reflects the graph about the x-axis.
A transformation of the form -g(2x) is a reflection in the x axis together with a horizontal compression by a factor of 2.
Multiplying all inputs by minus 1 reflects the graph about the y-axis (i6: f(-x)).
A 4 to 20 mA transmitter is calibrated for offset and gain (i6: gain is the stretch, offset the lift).
In a composition of functions the output of one function becomes the input of another.
For differential-pressure flow, a signal that is 50% pressure difference at 12 mA goes through a square root to become 71% flow: one function's output feeds the next.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit includes deriving and evaluating composite functions.
An inverse function is the original function in reverse; for a function that multiplies by 3 and subtracts one, the inverse adds one and then divides by 3.
Not all functions have an inverse; only one-to-one functions do.
A horizontal line cutting a graph more than once, as it does for y = x², shows a many-to-one function, which by the rule above has no inverse.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit includes determining inverse functions of a range of functions and graphing functions with their inverses.
